rationale: RFC_029 §10.13 STEP 4 (owner-ruled sequence A, 2026-08-18): fix the surviving resolver shape-conflict AT SOURCE. After the v1.0.1315 roll the conflict population is ONE candidate set (measured 2026-08-19 12:16→16:08Z: 23 rows, 100% of the class): page-content-writer's generate_content step requests `current_page` (its prompt reads {{.current_page.title}} — it needs the page RECORD), and the resolver's whole-tree search collects the record at input_data.current_page / ~unwrap.current_page AND the page NAME STRING that build_render_context files under render_context.current_page and build_render_context.current_page (same step output, filed under output_field and step name). Two TYPES share one key in one collected_data tree; reflect.DeepEqual says they differ; a RESOLVER_CONFLICTING_CANDIDATES row is written on EVERY run. The winner is always the record (bugs_open/306's declared tie-break pins it), so no page was ever wrong — but this is a permanent false-positive population that blocks step 5 (conflicts → refusal) for ever: refusing would strip the page record from generate_content in 100% of runs. THE FIX: one name for the object, another for the string, at the boundary where they met. RenderContext's json tag is the SINGLE declaration of a field's template key (bugs_open/109) and therefore also its step-boundary key; this change introduces a small, reasoned rename map — renderContextStepContractRenames = {"current_page": "current_page_name"} — applied symmetrically at the two ends of the step contract: renderCtxToMap EMITS the page name as current_page_name (and refuses to re-emit the old key from the ContentData merge that follows), setRenderContextScalarsFromData READS current_page_name first and tolerates a STRING under the old spelling for trees written before the roll (read side only). The TEMPLATE contract is deliberately NOT renamed: components still read {{.current_page}} (the struct field is projected under its tag on the render side), because there the key is unambiguous, it is advertised to component authors, and renaming it would have to be coordinated with a live template edit across a roll. The rerender path's hand-built base map (buildRerenderBaseData, the restore contract's second producer) moves to the step name via the same helper; render_content_envelope_guard's identity chain gains render_context.current_page_name AHEAD of the old path, which stays for pre-roll trees. CONSUMERS ENUMERATED (2026-07-29 §3 — named and told, not merely measured): readers of the STEP-BOUNDARY key — Go: renderEnvelopeIdentity (updated here), mergeIntoRenderContext's four call sites (all go through the symmetric restore), buildRerenderBaseData (updated here); config: 0 of the live agent_definitions mention render_context.current_page or build_render_context.current_page; readers of the TEMPLATE key (unaffected): 1 of 306 content_components across every component_level (evidence-chart, `$page := .current_page`), 0 of 265 component_versions, 0 Go-embedded templates, 0 agent prompts advertising {{.current_page}} as a bare variable; structuralFields in v3_site_actions.go still lists current_page, correctly. PROOF: 7 tests pin both halves and were mutation-proved SIX ways (emit under the template key; drop the ContentData skip; drop the legacy read fallback; drop the step-name read; base map under the old key; envelope chain without the new path — each fails a NAMED test; package compiles throughout). Plus a test at the resolver seam itself: the real datahelpers.ExtractFields over a live-shaped tree with renderCtxToMap's real output records ZERO conflicts and returns the record, and a CONTROL with the pre-rename shape still records one (the instrument is proven live in the test, so the zero is not a silent instrument). REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: (a) rename the json tag itself — renames the template contract as a side effect (structuralFields, evidence-chart, every future author), needs a live template edit ordered against the roll, and widens scope into a namespace with no defect; (b) a type-aware search (accept only map-shaped current_page) — bakes schema knowledge into a shared resolver, wider blast radius than renaming one key at one producer; (c) a `!` strict marker — impossible, generate_content's request list is Go-side. Behaviour change is confined to the step output key; every template sees exactly what it saw. Inert until the next chassis roll; the done-condition is RFC_029 §10.13 step 4's: the pcw `current_page` conflict class reads ZERO in the post-roll window against live demand (pcw runs present), after which step 5 is buildable.

plan.risks: (1) Trees in flight across the roll hold render_context.current_page (string) written by the old binary and are restored by the new one — covered by the read-side tolerance (TestRestoreAcceptsBothSpellingsAcrossTheRoll 'old tree' case) and the envelope chain keeping the old path; the html/template path would also survive on the ContentData catch-all alone. (2) A NEW string candidate could appear if some other step files a `current_page` string into collected_data — the resolver-seam test and the post-roll window read (same query as grounded_in[0]) are the detectors; today's population is exactly one set and this change ends it. (3) The tolerance keeps `current_page` as an ACCEPTED restore key, which a reader could mistake for a sanctioned emit name — the comment on setRenderContextScalarsFromData says read-side-only, and TestStepOutputNeverCarriesCurrentPage makes an emit under the old name a failing test. (4) Templates now ALSO receive `.current_page_name` via the ContentData catch-all on restore (every step-output key does, e.g. _sources_merged) — harmless extra key; `.current_page` is unchanged. (5) NOT a config change and NOT a template change: nothing to order against the roll; inert until the next chassis build. Verification after the roll: stamp the binary (known-absent + known-present controls), then the grounded_in[0] query over the post-roll window must read 0 rows for pcw/current_page against live pcw demand (orchestrations referencing page-content-writer in the window); a zero with no pcw runs is not evidence.
